name: Varbase Media Demo Assets
description: Provides pre-set default media assets for Varbase Media types (for dev/testing/demos).
project_description:
Provide a pre-set of default media assets for all Varbase Media Types, which are needed in development, testing, and demos.

 Using the Varbase Media and Varbase Media Demo Assets modules in Varbase or installed with any Drupal site. Even if installed with the Minimal or Standard profile.

 
 Having to upload files, images, local videos, and remote videos ( YouTube, Vimeo ) media entities. 
 And set them in every round for Development , Testing , and Demos . 
 Which are needed for Varbase Storybook use. 
 
 
 Enable the module by Drush ( or install it from the UI)

 

drush en varbase_media_demo

 

 Open the site with the browser and navigate to "/admin/content/media-grid" 

 Media Library Grid view 1 

 

 

 

 Media Library Grid view 2 

 

 

 

 Media Library - Images 

 

 

 

 Media Library - Remote Videos 

 

 

 

 Media Library - Local Videos 

 

 

 

 
 Saving time on Development , Testing , and Demos .

This is the full set of Varbase Options for Media types. Including Videos without cover images and with cover images.

 
Once the installation process is complete, you can safely remove the Varbase Media Demo Assets module. This module has already served its purpose by providing the necessary media demo assets during setup, but it is no longer required for the Varbase Demo site. To uninstall it, you can execute the following commands:
 Using Drush: 

 drush pm:uninstall varbase_media_demo 

 Additionally, you can remove it from your Composer dependencies: 

 composer remove drupal/varbase_media_demo 

 By following these steps, you can keep your Varbase Demo site clean and efficient, only retaining the essential components needed for your project.

 
 

 
 

 Use With Varbase Distribution: 
 This module is best used with Varbase distribution.

 Can be installed with any Drupal 9/10/11 site. Even if installed with the Minimal or Standard profile.

 However, using it with Varbase gives you way much more cool stuff!
